solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pedant thus restricts small children — only one left in charge

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the word for thus closes around the next piece

parts.note: thus means so, as in 'and so it was'
small children is the short form, CH, the standard abbreviation for children
the only one left is the last one

explanation.surface: A fussy schoolmaster keeps the little ones in check until just one remains, and that one is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedant' here is a noun: a scholastic is a hair-splitting academic, so the answer is used as a noun, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholastic, as a noun, is a schoolman given to over-subtle hair-splitting, which is exactly a pedant.

clue.text: Horsey person brings coin to one ancient city

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
one gives A, the indefinite article
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A horsy type brings a coin to an ancient city, like a tourist at a ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur in Greek myth is half man and half horse, so quite literally a horsey person.

clue.text: Roman poet holds ball shaped like rugger ball?

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A Roman poet clutches a ball the shape of a rugby ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby ball is egg-shaped, and ovoid means egg-shaped; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Lover's run inside with her topless military man

indicators.note: the run goes inside the word for lover

parts.note: an amour is a lover or love affair; the possessive adds no letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: topless means the word her loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A lover's dash indoors with a topless woman: a racy scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An armourer is a soldier who maintains and repairs weapons, so a military man by trade.

clue.text: Pretension and truth interchangeable in certain manoeuvres

indicators.note: letters that are interchangeable can be swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that pretension and truth can be swapped in some dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-point turns are the driving manoeuvres used to turn a car round in a narrow road.

clue.text: Husband in robe left here to worship

indicators.note: the husband goes in the robe

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless robe or cloak

explanation.surface: A husband in a robe has come to this place to pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, so a place one comes to worship.

clue.text: Highland town one adding fuel to flame

definitions.meaning: A town in Caithness in the Scottish Highlands
a candle's string draws molten wax up to feed the flame

explanation.surface: A Highland town is the troublemaker who adds fuel to the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is both a northern Scottish town and the cord in a candle that carries fuel to its flame.

clue.text: Humour and derisive exclamation given by Shakespeare vigorously

parts.note: wit is humour
ha! is a scornful exclamation
Will is Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: Humour and mockery delivered energetically by the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with a will means doing it energetically and with determination, an idiom for vigorously.

clue.text: See greatest boxer tops outlaw monster

indicators.note: in a down clue, the boxer is placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: the letter C is spoken like the word see, a familiar crossword substitution
Muhammad Ali called himself the Greatest
to ban is to outlaw

explanation.surface: Look: the greatest boxer beats a monster outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the savage, deformed creature in Shakespeare's The Tempest, often called a monster in the play.

clue.text: Open party Ban Ki-moon gives?

parts.note: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations, the UN
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An open party that the UN Secretary-General throws.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'party Ban Ki-moon gives' is a UN do, a United Nations party.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a parcel or a knot is to open it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Commercial mail centre destroyed

indicators.note: the destroyed words fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A commercial mail sorting office has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to trade and merchants, so commercial.

clue.text: Deliver gold in horse-drawn carriage

parts.note: to land a blow is to deliver it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An instruction to deliver gold by horse and carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top, an example of the type.

clue.text: Sheep or small black ram we returned?

indicators.note: returned means the whole string of pieces is read from the back

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a ram is a male sheep, so male

explanation.surface: A shepherd's question: are these sheep, or is it a little black ram we brought back?
explanation.definitionFit: Female young sheep are sheep, a plural example matching the plural answer.

clue.text: Magician puts sulphur in right hole

indicators.note: sulphur is put in the word for right

parts.note: proper means right or correct
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a hole is round, like O

explanation.surface: A conjuror drops sulphur into exactly the right hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero is the exiled duke and sorcerer of Shakespeare's The Tempest, a famous stage magician.

clue.text: Islander collapsed drain to stop Irish girl

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the rearranged drain sits inside the girl's name

parts.note: Sian is a girl's name (strictly Welsh, as a blog commenter noted)

indicators.note: a collapsed drain is broken up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken drain blocks the way of an Irish girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Sian is in fact a Welsh name, not Irish, a slip the blog accepted; the girl's name still gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is a native of Sardinia, the Mediterranean island, so an islander.

clue.text: Legal institutions in north and south

explanation.surface: Legal bodies found throughout the country, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inns of Court are the four London societies that train and call barristers to the English bar.

clue.text: Travel in space is male fantasy

indicators.note: the letters of space travel about, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Space travel is a man's daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is retreat into fantasy and daydreams away from real life.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: the answer is taken in by the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A drug addict is taken into care because of a relapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug taker, so an addict.

clue.text: Witch discontented Savoy Company getting artist cross

indicators.note: with its contents gone, the word Savoy keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: An unhappy Savoy opera company finds its artist angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy Company evokes Gilbert and Sullivan's D'Oyly Carte troupe at London's Savoy Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycorax is the witch, Caliban's mother, spoken of but never seen in The Tempest.

clue.text: Say Latin may require thinner voice?

indicators.note: the letters may require rearranging, a loose signal to reorder them

explanation.surface: Speaking Latin may call for a reedier tone of voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasality is a twangy quality of speech through the nose, which sounds thin and reedy.

clue.text: English politician in tax storm

indicators.note: the English politician goes in the word for tax

parts.note: to tax someone is to test or strain them
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A storm breaks over an English politician's tax affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm; it is also the title of the play behind this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Food given outside theatre off trolley

indicators.note: the food is given on the outside, wrapped around the theatre

parts.note: a meal is food
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: Food handed out in front of a theatre off a trolley, like an interval snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Off one's trolley is a British idiom for mad, which mental means in colloquial use.

clue.text: West's mishap having replaced leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the mishap word is swapped for another letter

parts.note: an accident is a mishap

explanation.surface: The western world's misfortune after a change of leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the leader A; the definition settles that it is O. The 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the western world, the West as opposed to the Orient.

clue.text: After time in dust mum's wheezing

indicators.note: mum's word comes after the dust piece
time is placed in the word for dust

parts.note: ash is dust from burning
ma is mum; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: After a spell in a dusty room, Mum is wheezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog wondered whether 'wheezing' alone is enough for the definition; the whole clue reads as a cause of the condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is the chest condition whose main symptom is wheezing, so the definition is by symptom.

clue.text: Athenian misanthrope has army doctor split money

indicators.note: the army doctor splits the money word apart by sitting in it

parts.note: tin is British slang for money
an MO, Medical Officer, is an army doctor

explanation.surface: An army doctor and a misanthrope share out the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's play about a rich Athenian who turns against humanity.

clue.text: Our tribe AC/DC rocked to the City and the World

definitions.text: to the City and the World

indicators.note: rocked means shaken up, so the letters are rearranged; a nod to the rock band

parts.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: Our tribe was rocked by the band AC/DC.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbi et orbi is Latin for to the city of Rome and to the world, the Pope's blessing.

clue.text: Hounds assembly that's correct

definitions.meaning: the gathering of huntsmen and hounds before a fox hunt
... in old use means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that the hounds are assembling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunt's gathering is a meet, and the archaic adjective meet means right or proper.

clue.text: Animals driven from Rio Xenxem

indicators.note: the letters are driven out of the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Animals herded out of some invented place called Rio Xenxem.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle used for draught work, an example of animals.

clue.text: Thrown at me, insult done at 23:59?

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at me at the eleventh hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at 23:59 is done a minute before midnight, the final moment before a deadline.
